jobs.description:
Amazon Business customers buy at a scale most retail systems were never built for: a school district ordering 2,000 chairs, a contractor ordering 900 boxes of fasteners, a hospital restocking an entire floor. Today those orders often arrive as dozens of separate boxes over many days, and we are rebuilding how Amazon fulfills them.
You will own the product roadmap for bulk and large order fulfillment at Amazon Business. The goal is simple to state and hard to build: a customer places one large order, picks one date, and receives it once, in the form factor that fits their dock and their crew. Getting there means changing how Amazon sources, consolidates, packs and ships large orders, working shoulder to shoulder with the engineering teams that own fulfillment planning and fulfillment center operations. This is a builder role with a funded roadmap and direct exposure to senior leaders across Amazon Business, supply chain and operations.

Key job responsibilities
Own the product roadmap for bulk and large order fulfillment, from customer problem through launch and measured outcome.
Write the documents that get the work funded and built: PRFAQs, business requirements documents, and annual and three year planning inputs.
Act as the requirements owner with partner engineering teams in fulfillment planning and fulfillment center technology, not a ticket filer. Negotiate scope, sequence and dependencies directly with their product and engineering leaders.
Define how Amazon consolidates a large order into as few deliveries as possible, including palletized delivery and customer selected delivery dates.
Define how a request for many individual units can be served from cases and pallets of the same product, working through the inventory, receive and pick changes that requires.
Build the case for dedicated bulk fulfillment capacity, including moving product from suppliers to customers without a putaway step.
Replace manual operator work with automation across sourcing, consolidation and promise, and track the reduction.
Own the metrics: deliveries per order, delivery date accuracy, ship cost per unit and contribution profit per unit. Pull your own data and defend your own numbers.

A day in the life
You will spend your day between customers and builders. Mornings often start in the data, checking how last week's large orders actually shipped and where they fragmented. From there it is working sessions with fulfillment planning and fulfillment center engineering teams on requirements, a review with operations leaders on the manual work still left in the flow, and time with Amazon Business sales and customer teams on what large buyers are asking for. You will write often, and you will present what you write to directors and above.

Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋

We're looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager to join our Product & Technology Operations team and own how we build the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC) into a shared execution model across Product, Engineering, and Design.

You will own how work flows from idea to impact across the organization - one language for how work moves, one set of metrics leaders can trust, and one standard for what "good" looks like at every stage of PDLC.

This is a founding role for the function. You'll define the model, align stakeholders around it, and prove out its value as you build.

What you’ll be doing:

Define the execution model

 - Design a PDLC framework that works across Product, Engineering, and Design and across all Lightspeed products.

 - Define what good looks like at each stage of PDLC, including the artifacts, checkpoints, and exit criteria teams should use.

Build the measurement system

 - Establish metrics that give leaders a trustworthy, holistic view of how work is flowing and where it's getting stuck.

 - Design the framework so it measures the system and surfaces bottlenecks, not individual performance.

 - Build in exception tracking so blocked or off-track work is visible early.

Drive adoption

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders across every vertical to align on the model and earn genuine buy-in and adoption.

 - Navigate real differences across verticals and business units without forcing false consistency where it doesn't make sense.

 - Bring structure to ambiguity - resolve open questions as they surface rather than waiting for a perfect spec.

Build an AI-first PDLC

 - Define what humans own versus what AI agents own at each stage of PDLC, keeping judgment, accountability, and anything irreversible or customer-facing with humans.

 - Partner with Engineering to identify where AI agents can accelerate delivery, build pilots, and measure their ROI and impact on speed.

 - Ensure human checkpoints are genuine decisions, not rubber stamps, as adoption scales.

Evolve the model

 - Treat the framework as a living system - review it periodically and adjust based on what's actually working.

 - Report on program health and progress to senior leadership.
